previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for HCV cirrhosis, chronic kidney disease, diabetes, and essential tremor was admitted due to dehydration and acute kidney injury following two weeks of diarrhea and poor oral intake. She presented with elevated creatinine, hyperkalemia, and non-anion gap metabolic acidosis. IV fluids were administered, leading to improvement in renal function. Diarrhea resolved during admission, and stool studies were negative for common pathogens. Tacrolimus levels were initially elevated, prompting a dose reduction to 1 mg twice daily, with instructions to monitor levels post-discharge. CMV, viral, and parasitic studies were negative. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans to follow up on hepatitis C treatment eligibility given improved kidney function and to monitor tacrolimus levels closely.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ y/o female with a past medical history of HCV 
cirrhosis c/b ___ s/p liver transplant c/b recurrent HCV,

# Diarrhea in immunocompromised host: The patient reported a ___ 
week history of non-bloody diarrhea, occurring right after 
eating, without associated fevers of chills. The patient had 
been evaluated in liver clinic with stool studies which were 
negative for C diff, as well as E coli, Yersenia, campylobacter, 
salmonella, shigella and CMV viral load was negative. The 
patient was evaluated with giardia and cryptosporidium stool 
studies which were negative, norovirus PCR which was negative, 
as well as 2 additional O+Ps which were pending at the time of 
discharge. The patient's diarrhea resolved spontaneously on 
admission. The etiology of the patient's diarrhea remained 
unclear, possibly secondary to tacrolimus vs. gastroenteritis. 
The patient was volume resuscitated as below and should f/u with 
hepatology for further evaluation and management. 
 
# Acute on chronic kidney disease: The patient was found to have 
baseline Cr 1.6-2.0, elevated to Cr 2.2 on admission. ___ was 
thought to be pre-renal in the setting of ongoing diarrhea. The 
patient was treated with IV albumin and her Cr improved to 1.2 
on the day of discharge. The patient's home tacrolimus was held 
x1 dose and was restarted at 1mg PO q12hrs. The patient's home 
nadolol and Lasix were held as below. The patient should f/u 
with hepatology for further dosing of tacrolimus and further 
monitoring of level (last tacro level at discharge 3.8, kept at 
same dose in the setting of changing Cr.)  

# Leukopenia, anemia: The patient was found to have WBC 2.0 and 
Hgb 8.0 from 3.4 and 10 respectively on the second day of 
admission after aggressive IVF and albumin administration. This 
was thought to be dilutional as all cell lines were depressed. 
The patient should have repeat CBC after discharge for further 
monitoring. 

# HCV cirrhosis c/b HCC s/p liver transplant c/b recurrent HCV, 
cirrhosis: The patient's home nadolol was held in the setting of 
___. Her Lasix was also held given likely pre-renal etiology of 
___. The patient's nadolol was started once she had recovering 
of kidney function. The patient should f/u with hepatology to 
determine when to restart Lasix. The patient was continued on 
home harvoni and tacrolimus as above. 

# Seizure disorder: continued home keppra 

# Hypertension: continued home amlodipine. 

# Diabetes: continued glargine and ISS
